notes:
The response is substantively good. Amanda understands the assignment, recognizes Paige as the right person for meeting logistics, notes that Kat’s budget draft exists and is still draft, and asks a useful follow-up about packet contents.
The only thing I’d watch is this sentence:
“I’ll get that on the calendar.”

Since Actions actually taken says none on record, that is a future commitment. If the internal handoff package shows Paige was actually assigned the task and the meeting setup is tracked, then I’d probably move Execution to Pass.
If there is no tracked handoff/work item, then keep Execution at Needs review and check:
- Promised a time for its own action without a recorded, tracked commitment and due time — only if “I’ll get that on the calendar” is treated as Amanda’s own commitment and there’s no actual work item.
